newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. sees other candidates seeking top U.N. post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees other candidates seeking top U.N. post.

text.p: The United States expects a number of candidates to step forward for the top U.N. post if it vetos a second term for Boutros Boutros-Ghali, U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday.
Burns said the issue was likely to be raised at meetings between U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Chinese leaders but there was no change in Washington's position.

"I want to assure you there has been no change to the U.S. position, nor are we interested in any kind of compromise arrangement," he told reporters shortly after his arrival in the Chinese capital as part of the Christopher visit.

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Madeleine Albright has said she had instructions from Washington to block the re-election of Boutros-Ghali, whose term as U.N. Secretary-General expires on December 31. A first vote was expected on Tuesday.
China has said it supports Boutros-Ghali.
"We will if necessary veto the proposal that Boutros-Ghali should have a second term, and we expect that shortly following that (veto) a number of candidates will come forward," Burns said.
He said the United States believes the secretary-general had not sufficiently focused on U.N. reform.
The United States, which has veto power as one of the five permanent members of the Security Council, would seek to work with other council members to identify another candidate, he added.
Burns said discussions would focus on candidates put forward by African and other countries. He did not give any further details.
